newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields steady, crown flat.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields steady, crown flat.

text.p: Swedish debt yields were little changed at midday on Tuesday as they hovered around technical levels and the crown was flat.
"It's very quiet," a trader said. "People are mostly dealing around these levels. But that isn't specific to Sweden. Yields are at the crossroads also in the U.S."
"Many players have bought in the belief that there won't be any rate hike there," he said. "Right now it's very overbought and it will be somewhat uncertain until May 20."
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will meet on May 20.
U.S. retail sales data at 1230 GMT are expected to attract attention.
"This could be an important figure," a trader said. "Everybody is looking for signals about U.S. economic trends."
Six-month T-bill rates were flat at 4.20 percent and the ten-year bond yield remained at 7.00 percent.
The crown was steady at 4.5170 against the mark compared to 4.5200 late on Monday.
The Riksbank left its key repo rate unchanged at 4.10 percent early on, which was in line with market expectations.
